rubric.note: New geometry (corridor.glb sha256 3d9de824..., 1,946 low / 11,939 high tris, was 1,912 / 11,863). Fixed: the dropped end-bay soffit box that read as a gable hood is gone. A chamfered corridor_rib now follows the cove and the vault (3x crop of hero x 530-750, y 160-320), so the vault line is continuous to the end wall. The chamfered walnut vault, moulded wall panels between pilasters and the calm wallpaper scale still hold. Still open: it is still a straight 2 x 8 m tube with no jog, niche or alcove, so the only spatial events are the three ribs and the lanterns. New, small: the pilaster capital blocks under the end rib read as pale cream wedges (left capital region RGB 91,64,44 with p90 L* 58), lighter than any other walnut in the frame, so they look like a different material at the rib springing.

Fixed: the 8 m floor now has a feature. floor_inlay lays two brass-aged runs with cross bands (visible at hero rows 520 and 655 and in the lamp shot), and they lead the eye to the far door. The light-dark rhythm along the floor holds: hero floor strip x 560-720 runs L* 26.3 at row 510, 49.2 at row 585 and 32.5 at row 705 (pool/gap 1.87 on this profile). The seam shot still opens onto the hall (hall interior through the door RGB 51,28,20, L* 13.4) with its floor sigil and chandelier visible, so the passage arrives somewhere. Per the orchestrator's ruling, the sealed cap (RGB 0,0,0 in p5-rooms-corridor-floor-sealed-north.jpg, x 530-745, y 200-540, from the proof path that skips dressSealedDoors) is judged as a walnut leaf, and the open-door voids in the single-room hero and lamp shots (RGB 14,10,7) are not counted. Still open: the lanterns no longer read as candle lanterns. The glass is a uniform cream panel (hero lantern RGB 232,224,182, hue 58, saturation 0.23) with no flame or warm core visible in a 4x crop, so the passage's light sources read as electric fixtures.

Fixed: the lamp-camera pilaster side face no longer smears. In a 2x crop of lamp x 1120-1280 it shows proper vertical grain; it is lighter than the front face (side RGB 105,55,29, L* 28.7; front 58,37,29, L* 16.9), and Blender lamp.lightmapped.png shows the same side at 97,52,27, so that difference is baked light, not a UV fault. Wainscot grain, ceiling boards, panel mouldings and floor stone all read. Lightmap holds at 124.5 px/m mean, 105.7 min, 568 UV1 islands, 0 px overlap, 16 px min gap (was 20), 2.0% clipping. Still open, moved from bake to runtime: the end rib's face is a grey-mauve band in the full engine frame (hero x 600-690, y 180-190: RGB 69,53,48, saturation 0.32), while the same pixels are walnut in the lightmap-only frame (42,19,6, saturation 0.86) and in the Cycles diffuse reference (43,19,7). So the runtime adds a grey probe or specular sheen to that face. The old soffit had the same mauve read, so the colour came back on the new geometry. Gilt door jambs are brighter after 581c631 (top quartile RGB 198,171,129) but sit at hue 35, saturation 0.36, a pale champagne against the bible's polished brass #DEC16A (hue 44, saturation 0.52). The floor grout lines are heavy and dark (2x crop), which pushes the stone towards a cartoon tile.

Fixed, mostly: the red monochrome is gone. Frame mean saturation is 0.727 on the pinned jpg (0.717 on engine.hero.png), down from 0.88. That is now at the study's level: the re-shot study engine hero is 0.736 and p5-int-study.jpg is 0.637. Walnut moved from hue 5-9 at saturation 0.95-0.97 to hue 13-17 at saturation 0.87-0.90 (left wainscot RGB 38,12,4; ceiling 57,22,8). That matches the in-game study wainscot (p5-int-study.jpg, hue 17.4, saturation 0.88). It is still redder than the bible's oiled walnut #583C26 (hue 26, saturation 0.57), but that albedo is shared with the study. Value: mean L* 18.0, 13.7% of pixels below L* 5, p90 39.1. That is brighter than the study engine hero re-shot at 60cff33 (L* 11.7, 39.9% below L* 5) and darker than p5-int-study.jpg (24.0). Still open: the wallpaper ground on the near right wall is RGB 44,11,5 at saturation 0.91, hue 10.5 (the left wall is 58,22,12 at 0.80). The builder's 0.749 is a frame-region figure, not the ground. New, and a bible conflict: the desaturation was bought by moving the lantern light to near white (report.json bake_lights colour 1.0, 0.92, 0.82, glass transmit 1.0, 1.0, 1.0), while the bible makes candle amber #F3BE65 the light colour of candles and lamps. The light pools on the walls also read as hard-edged hourglass shapes, not soft pools. Lamp row 360 jumps from L* 17 to 40-70 within 8 px and drops from 43 to 15 within 4 px, and the same shape repeats under every lantern in all four shots. I weighted the engine shots. The lightmap-only frame (saturation 0.726, L* 16.7) and Cycles diffuse reference (0.703, 18.2) show that both the near-white light and the cone shape are baked, while the rib sheen is added at runtime.

rubric.criterion: readability and comfort at seated VR distance
rubric.note: Black crush stays low: 13.7% of hero pixels are below L* 5 and 2.5% below L* 2. The lamp and seam shots are at 9.4% and 9.3% below L* 5. The motif scale is calm and no moire showed in 2-3x crops. Still open: the near-left wainscot is L* 6.4 (p10 3.8), below the L* 8 target the previous review set. New: the hard cone edges (an L* jump of 25-50 within 4-8 px, at every lantern, at eye height) are now the highest-contrast edges on the walls. In a headset they will be the first thing the eye lands on along the walls, and they may crawl with head motion. A desktop shot cannot settle the headset result.

topFixes: Put candle amber back in the lanterns without bringing the red back. Give the glass a visible warm core or flame card (target glass hue 35-45 at saturation 0.45-0.6, near #F3BE65, instead of today's cream RGB 232,224,182 at saturation 0.23). Keep the bake's light energy near-neutral if needed to hold frame saturation at 0.72 or below, so the source reads as candle amber even if the bounce stays pale.

Soften the wall light pools. Raise spot_blend on the three lantern_*_pool spots well above 0.35, or move the spot origin below the lantern cap so the cap no longer cuts a hard hourglass shadow. Target: a cone edge transition of 20 px or more at hero distance instead of 4-8 px, giving the soft pools the bible asks for.

Remove the runtime grey sheen on the end rib face (RGB 69,53,48 at saturation 0.32 in the engine against 42,19,6 in the lightmap-only frame). Lower that face's probe and specular contribution or roughness response so it stays walnut. In the same pass, darken the cream pilaster capital blocks to walnut, and lift the near-left wainscot to L* 8 or above.
independentScore.method: Read the brief, docs/art-bible.md, and the previous review (score 74 at ac21f3b) in /tmp/rxr-prev/score-corridor-v3.json, which matches provenance.json independentScore. Read the builder's /tmp/rxr-prev/rebake2-status.md and treated its claims as claims to check. I re-measured its saturation and wallpaper figures myself and got different values for the wallpaper ground. Viewed all five corridor engine jpgs (hero, hero.diffuse, lamp, floor-sealed-north, seam-from-corridor, dated 2026-11-17 09:37), the review sheet, the study engine hero re-shot at 60cff33, and p5-int-study.jpg. Measured with Pillow and numpy (CIE L*, HSV hue and saturation): frame mean L*, p10/p90, the share below L* 5 and below L* 2, and frame saturation for every corridor engine and Blender render and for the study references. Took region stats for both wainscots, ceiling, floor near/mid/far, the door void, gilt jamb (with its top quartile), lantern glass, end rib face, pilaster capitals, banner, both wallpapers (ground and motif split at the 30th and 85th L* percentiles), the lamp-shot pilaster side and front faces, the hall seen through the seam door and the sealed cap. Took a floor L* profile in 15 px rows and horizontal L* profiles through the lamp-shot light cone. Made 2-4x Lanczos crops of the hero end bay, hero floor, hero lantern, lamp cone, lamp right edge (engine and Blender lamp.lightmapped), seam door and sealed door. Compared the rib face and walnut across the full engine frame, lightmap-only frame and Cycles diffuse reference to separate bake from runtime. Read report.json (bake lights, bounces, densities, clipping), engine-compare.json and uv1-report.json. Confirmed that the corridor.glb sha256 matches report.json, uv1-report.json and the builder's report. Weighted the engine shots; Blender renders were used only to attribute faults. Applied the orchestrator's rulings: sealed caps are judged as walnut leaves, and open-door voids in single-room shots are not counted. Read-only on the repo. Scripts are in /tmp/rxr-prev/v4c/.
